payload.text: Stability of the noise, not presence of it, decides gradeability, and the repeat count that establishes it is PER SLIDE and ADAPTIVE rather than a global constant. A single --repeats over every slide is itself a population error: measured 2026-09-09, slides 13 and 17 were clean across all fifteen pairs while slide 14 was bimodal, so one number either over-captures nineteen slides or under-captures one. The mechanism captures a slide until either its stability is established at the stated confidence or a difference appears -- at which point the slide is known unstable and the run is measuring its floor rather than establishing stability. Cheap for clean slides, costly only for genuinely unstable ones. Same shape as AC-2.12 (an outcome, not a parameter) applied to a different variable: that row is about capture TIMING, this one about capture COUNT. THE RATE IS COUNTED, NOT FITTED: hashing the captures makes the modes directly observable, and a 5/1 split of six yields exactly the 5-of-15 differing pairs measured, which confirms the two-mode model structurally instead of assuming it. A rate inferred through the pair count inverts a quadratic with two roots and compounds sampling error. NO FLOOR IS CITABLE from a run predating 6c278a2, nor from the corrected control (2 repeats), nor from any count derived from a six-capture sample, whose 95 percent interval on a 1/6 minority spans roughly 0.4 to 64 percent.
